I am 64 years old. I have farmed these 8.5 mu in Quzhou County for 45 years. I never went to school. Everything I know I learned from my father and from watching the neighbors. My family has seven people, and my sons send some money from working outside, but the farm is still what feeds us.

This year I will plant 7 mu with wheat and then maize, and 1.5 mu with cotton. That is the same as last year. I do not change what works.

For the wheat: I sowed last October with improved seed from the shop — the kind in the red bag that my neighbor Lao Wang used and said was good. Before sowing I rotary tilled the ground. I put one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer on each mu as base. In the spring I will topdress with one 40-jin bag of urea per mu. I know that is a good amount because two years ago I tried to save half a bag on the east field and the wheat turned yellow and the ears were small. I will irrigate three times from my well: once when the wheat turns green, once when it shoots up tall, and once when the grain is filling. I will spray twice — once for grass and once when the aphids come in May. If the weather is like last year I will get about 550 kg per mu.

For the maize: After I cut the wheat in June, I plant hybrid maize seed straight into the stubble without tilling again. The machine man charges less that way and I save three days, which matters because the summer season is short before the cold comes. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then when the plants are knee-high I spread one bag of urea per mu. I will irrigate twice — once after sowing if it is dry, and once when the tassels come out. I spray twice, for weeds and corn borer. I expect 600 kg per mu.

For the cotton: I keep 1.5 mu of cotton because Lao Zhang got a good price last year and the ginnery is not too far. In spring I plough deep because cotton roots need loose soil. I plant hybrid Bt cotton seed. I use one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and half a bag of urea later when the flowers open. I irrigate three times: after sowing, at flowering, and when the bolls are fat. Cotton always has bugs, so I spray four times. I expect about 250 kg per mu of seed cotton.

Fertilizer costs a lot this year. Every bag is real money. But last year when I tried to save one bag on the east field, the yield dropped by more than that bag was worth. So I will use the same amounts. I would rather waste some fertilizer than risk an empty table. My neighbor does about the same, and I watch his fields too.
